2ff26f97a71862cf.title: Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 results: Net profit rises 1.25% to ₹312 crore
2ff26f97a71862cf.summary: Non-bank lender Sammaan Capital on Saturday reported a 1.25 per cent increase in its September quarter net profit to Rs 312.34 crore compared to Rs 308.47 crore in the same quarter of last year. The company had reported a net profit of Rs 243.30 crore in the preceding June quarter. Its total income declined to Rs 1,850.85 crore in the reporting quarter from Rs 2,260.52 crore in the year-ago period, which included a decline in the core interest income to Rs 1,161.26 crore from Rs 1,449.02 crore. Total expenses also declined to Rs 1,426.28 crore from Rs 1,835.49 crore in the year-ago period, as per a regulatory filing. Assets under management grew by 5 per cent to Rs 59,188 crore as of end-June 2026, driven by a 62 per cent jump in disbursements to Rs 6,278 crore. It aims to increase AUM to Rs 70,000 crore by March 2027. The company added more branches during the quarter to take its overall network to 245 as of September 30, and is aiming to take the same to 270 by end of the fiscal

752829ddf5823b16.title: Patanjali Foods Q2 FY27 results: Net profit falls 19% to ₹420 crore
752829ddf5823b16.summary: Patanjali Foods Ltd on Saturday reported 19 per cent fall in consolidated net profit at Rs 419.76 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 despite rise in revenue. Its net profit stood at Rs 516.69 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 11,406.49 crore in the second quarter of the current fiscal from Rs 9,850.06 crore a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. Total operational expenses went up to Rs 10,997.51 crore from Rs 9,344.97 crore. During the first six months of this fiscal, the net profit rose to Rs 755.49 crore from Rs 697.05 crore in the year-ago period. Total income grew to Rs 22,748.38 crore from Rs 18,629.08 crore. Incorporated in 1986, Patanjali Foods is one of the leading FMCG players in India. The company is present in edible oils, FMCG, and wind power generation segments. It sells products under different brands including Patanjali, Ruchi Gold, Nutrela, Dant Kanti, Mahakosh and Sunrich.

806f3ebdbf830649.title: Delhi govt notifies Aadhaar authentication for Unified Data Platform
806f3ebdbf830649.summary: The Delhi government has issued a notification to integrate Aadhaar-based data collection - part of its Unified Citizen Data Platform - to disburse benefits under its welfare scheme. 2b47ede68deb4619.title: CBI searches 33 locations in six states in Mahadev betting app case
2b47ede68deb4619.summary: The CBI has conducted searches at 33 locations across six states in connection with its investigation into Mahadev online betting app case, recovering digital devices, mobile phones and documents indicating the use of mule bank accounts and hawala channels, officials said on Saturday. The agency said the searches were conducted on the basis of disclosures made by Sourabh Chandrakar, one of the platform's principal promoters, following his extradition from Oman. The searches, carried out over the past few days, targeted premises linked to panel operators of the betting platform, they said. The CBI spokesperson said live betting and gambling panels were found operating at several locations and subsequently dismantled. Chandrakar was extradited from Oman and arrested by the CBI on November 1.

fa9c0dcaf9fec7e4.title: Vaishnaw stresses need for India to make own semiconductor machinery
fa9c0dcaf9fec7e4.summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday stressed the need for India to make its own machinery and high-precision components for semiconductor production, as the Centre works to build a robust domestic ecosystem for the sector. Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Information and Broadcasting, and Railways, made the remarks during a visit to the Ethereal Machines facility in Bengaluru, the PIB in Karnataka said in a post on X. He said the Centre, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was firmly committed to building a robust semiconductor ecosystem in the country. "In the spirit of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', as envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it is important that India develops and manufactures its own machines and high-precision components required for semiconductor manufacturing," he said. The Ethereal Machines facility was playing an important role in this direction by producing advanced machinery and high-precision components, he said.

7e89d9cac50ff30d.title: DPIIT, commerce department authorised to issue defence industrial licences
7e89d9cac50ff30d.summary: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and Department of Commerce (DoC) are the competent authorities to issue industrial licences for defence purposes, the commerce and industry ministry said. According to an official communication from DPIIT, both departments can issue these licences under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951. It stated that the industry department can issue licences for manufacturers located outside Special Economic Zones (SEZs), while the commerce department can issue licences for manufacturers located within these zones as well as for Export Oriented Units (EOUs). "It is reiterated that the following agencies (DPIIT and DoC) are competent to issue Industrial Licences for Defence purposes under the I (D&R) Act 1951, " DPIIT's press note said.

The air quality index (AQI) at 9 am stood at 348 (very poor), as compared to the 24-hour average AQI of 373 at 4 pm on Friday, according to data from the Central Board of Pollution Control (CPCB). As per the CPCB standards, an AQI of 0-50 is considered 'good', 51-100 'satisfactory', 101-200 'moderate', 201-300 'poor', 301-400 'very poor', and 401-500 'severe'. Out of the 59 air quality monitoring stations in the city, seven recorded AQI in the 'severe' category on Saturday morning. According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is expected to deteriorate further in the next few days. 2fad31e5af7a83b6.title: Trai bars 124,000 mobile connections in spam crackdown during July-Sep
2fad31e5af7a83b6.summary: Regulator TRAI took enforcement action against more than 1.24 lakh telecom resources and blacklisted 374 entities for one year for violating unsolicited commercial communication (UCC) norms during July-September, as it stepped up efforts to curb spam calls and messages. A total of 1,10,325 telecom resources, including mobile numbers, were barred from outgoing services for 15 days for the first violation, while 13,777 were disconnected for one year for repeat violations, according to TRAI's quarterly report for the second quarter of 2026-27. The regulator also blocked 3,725 SMS headers and blacklisted 374 senders for one year, during which they cannot obtain fresh telecom resources. TRAI received 15.29 lakh complaints of unsolicited commercial communications during the quarter, of which 7.23 lakh were classified as actionable. The complaints were registered against a backdrop of 714.01 billion calls and 702.28 billion SMSes originating from telecom networks across the country. The .

The 75-year-old former vice president was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday after he collapsed during his morning walk and remained unconscious for a few minutes. He was admitted to the hospital's Cardio-Neuro Centre and was under the care of the Department of Cardiology for medical evaluation and treatment. Security personnel accompanying Dhankhar had initially taken him home in a PCR vehicle after he collapsed. Later, he was admitted to AIIMS. Dhankhar has experienced several episodes of fainting and loss of consciousness over the past two years. But this time, the duration of loss of consciousness was the longest. In June 2025, he fainted during the golden jubilee celebrations of Kumaon University in Nainital. In January this year, he suffered two bouts of unconsciousness at home. Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit here, Noel said while "some people" are proposing a listing for the group's holding company, he fears that enlarging the number of shareholders after a listing will shift its focus to profits from philanthropy. "My worry is that listing, which is what some people are proposing, will change the Tata way. And one day, if we have 30,000-40,000 shareholders, profit may take precedence over philanthropy. And I think that will fundamentally change the Tata way of working," Noel, who turned 70 on Friday, was quoted as saying. "Tata Trusts will play a constructive role with regulators and others to try and find a solution which keeps the Tata way the way

The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to Rs 1,885.17 crore. With this, the affiliate's holding in Meesho has fallen to 5.19 per cent from 6.84 per cent. The stake sale, however, found buyers, with a clutch of domestic and foreign institutional investors participating in the transaction, with Societe Generale (SocGen) emerging as the largest buyer. Paris-based financial services firm SocGen picked up more than 1.47 crore shares, or a 0.32 per cent stake, for Rs 364.65 crore. The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to Rs 1,885.17 crore. With this, the affiliate's holding in Meesho has fallen to 5.19 per cent from 6.84 per cent. 8228d1c2a5e8563a.title: YMCA Madras launches IAS Academy for persons with hearing and speech disabilities
8228d1c2a5e8563a.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 05:30 am IST - Chennai YMCA Madras on Saturday launched an IAS Academy aimed at training persons with speech and hearing disabilities to face civil services examinations. Classes will be conducted at the YMCA Building on NSC Bose Road. The first batch will have 50 students, 43 of whom are speech and hearing impaired. For this year, YMCA Madras has tied up with St. Louis Institute for the Deaf and the Blind in Adyar. In the classroom, students will have support in the form of sign language specialists and a software that transcribes speech to text in real time. The initiative is part of YMCA’s MY Institute project that provides academic support, skill programmes, and sports and cultural activities for students. Inaugurating the academy, Justice P.T. Asha of the Madras High Court, said civil servants form the backbone of a government and the link between the Union and the States, the people, and the government. “The duty of an IAS officer is to ensure continuity in functioning of the government irrespective of the party in power,” she said, adding they are tasked with formulating and implementing policies. Irai Anbu, former Chief Secretary of Tamil Nadu, offered tips to the students for the UPSC examinations. He said their preparation should be structured and they should dedicate 12 hours a day for 400 days if they are to crack the civil services examinations. Albert Fernando, chairperson, MY Institute-IAS Academy, said that according to the 2011 Census and records available with the State Commissionerate for the Welfare of the Disabled, there were about 2,20,024 persons with hearing impairment, 80,077 persons with speech impairment, and 92,796 with both disabilities in Tamil Nadu. V. Nandakumar, Commissioner of Income Tax, and P. Asir Pandian, General Secretary and CEO, YMCA Madras, also spoke. 48277b4b616c3083.title: Take necessary steps to control inflation, Dhinakaran tells T.N. govt.
48277b4b616c3083.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:54 am IST - Chennai T.T.V. Dhinakaran | Photo Credit: R. ASHOK Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Saturday said Tamil Nadu ranks first in India in price rise and urged the TVK-led government to take necessary measures to control the surge in prices of essential commodities. Stating Tamil Nadu holds the top spot in India for price hikes as retail inflation in the State has risen to 7.29 per cent, Mr. Dhinakaran said this occurred as a result of negligence in monitoring the price rise and failing to take timely action to control it. “Without taking any steps to control the price rise of essential commodities, the TVK government merely watched as a bystander and was focused only on covering up the real situation, while now boasting that they have kept the prices of items including rice, sugar, and pulses under control and prevented hoarding,” he alleged. Mr. Dhinakaran said Tamil Nadu, which was once a pioneering state in India, has been pushed into an abyss over the past six months due to the inefficient administration of the TVK rule. He demanded that the government abandon efforts to divert the public through false propaganda on social media via “Paid Virtual Warriors,” and immediately undertake constructive measures necessary to control the price rise of essential commodities. 18214fc7b57a6fc9.title: Residents seek exemption of taxes for non-commercial vehicles at Pallikonda toll plaza
18214fc7b57a6fc9.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 05:30 am IST - VELLORE Residents in 12 farming villages have been demanding exemption of taxes at a toll plaza in Pallikonda town on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48), which is maintained by National Authority of India (NHAI). “The stretch helps reach government hospitals in big towns like Gudiyatham, Anaicut, Vellore towns easier. Exemption of toll should be given to locals, who are mostly marginal farmers and petty traders,” said B. Pasupathi, a resident. As per study, more than 75,000 vehicles, mainly trucks and container lorries, use the stretch to reach Chennai and Bengaluru every day. The stretch has at least 20 underpasses to allow residents to cross the stretch. It also has four toll plazas between Walajah (Ranipet) and Krishnagiri, a distance of 148 km. “Special passes at nominal rates have been provided to residents in surrounding villages. Complete waiver of toll fee for residents is not feasible,” a NHAI official told The Hindu . At present, residents within a 20-km-radius of Pallikonda toll plaza are provided with a monthly special pass for non-commercial vehicles, with a fee of ₹360. Vehicles should be registered with a local permanent address to avail special passes. “Most of the residents are farmers and tractors are not allowed to pass the toll plaza, as they have been classified as commercial vehicles. After harvest, a large number of tractors are roped in to transport paddy to government godowns in towns. The toll plaza should exempt vehicles that form part of farming activity,” said T. Veeraiyah, a farmer. Residents said complete exemption of toll fee will help them cut travel cost and boost agriculture in the area. 9f2018e6f5bfc5e6.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
9f2018e6f5bfc5e6.summary: Updated - November 15, 2026 04:02 am IST - Cape Canaveral SpaceX’s mega rocket Starship successfully returns to its launch pad and is caught by the launch tower following a test flight from Starbase, Texas, on November 14, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday (November 14, 2026), caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch. Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad. “Can you believe it?” shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot. SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique. NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars. The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-metre) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. 19c537da3dcfd703.title: Total Chess: Martirosyan inflicts first loss on Carlsen
19c537da3dcfd703.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:20 pm IST - BUDAPEST Martirosyan posted a win over World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen before drawing the return game. | Photo Credit: Flickr.com Magnus Carlsen suffered his first loss in the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot as Haik Martirosyan beat the World No. 1 and took the outright Group C lead on the third day of the Fast Classic stage here on Friday. The Armenian won with white before drawing their return encounter, leaving Carlsen winless after six games. Martirosyan had 10 points to Carlsen’s five. R. Vaishali secured her first Fast Classic victory, recovering from a defeat against Bibisara Assaubayeva to win their second meeting with an attack. The split results left the Indian on four points and the Kazakh on eight in Group D. Arjun Erigaisi overturned a difficult position to beat Wesley So with black before drawing the return match. His nine points put him level with Hans Niemann, three behind leader Maxime Vachier-Lagrave. R. Praggnanandhaa drew both games against Vladislav Artemiev in Group B, their first encounter lasting 89 moves. The Indian had four points and Artemiev five. Martirosyan’s attacking victory over Carlsen helped him move one point clear of Anish Giri, who followed a draw against Ian Nepomniachtchi with a win after a long battle. Nepomniachtchi and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov had seven points each. Mamedyarov drew twice against Abhimanyu Mishra, who had five. Vachier-Lagrave drew his game against Niemann before winning the return with white to reach 12 points. So had four. Group B leader Fabiano Caruana beat Vincent Keymer with black and drew their second game. Unbeaten with four wins and two draws, he had 14 points, four clear of Liem Le, who drew twice against Richard Rapport. Keymer had four points and Rapport five. In Group A, Andrew Hong handed Alireza Firouzja his first group-stage defeat before the leader won their return meeting. Firouzja retained top spot with 11 points. Hong had six. Jan-Krzysztof Du

7df78a651aea740f.title: Synod of Jacobite Church approves steps to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III
7df78a651aea740f.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST - KOCHI The Episcopal Synod of the Jacobite Syrian Church on Saturday (November 14) decided to complete the procedures to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III, who convened the historic Mulanthuruthy Synod in 1876. The decision was taken as Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, the supreme head of the Universal Syrian Orthodox Church, accepted the Jacobite Church’s request to declare Ignatius Peter III a saint. A statement by the Jacobite Syrian Church said the decision was taken at a meeting of the Episcopal Synod, chaired by Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, at the Marthoman Cathedral in Mulanthuruthy during the 150th anniversary celebrations of the Mulanthuruthy Synod. Addressing the synod, the Patriarch called for collective efforts to establish lasting peace in the Malankara Church. Hailing from Mosul, Ignatius Peter III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1872 until he died in 1894. a29277a425951066.title: Eight varieties of pharmaceutical ingredients worth ₹3.54 lakh seized in TG SAFE raid at Ameenpur firm
a29277a425951066.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 02:00 am IST - HYDERABAD The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district. The raid was conducted at Neocell Biotechnologies Private Limited, located at the Medical Devices Park in Sultanpur, on Friday, following credible information about the illegal stocking of pharmaceutical ingredients for sale without a valid drug licence. According to TG SAFE, officials found eight varieties of APIs illegally stocked at the premises and seized drug stocks worth ₹3.54 lakh. Further investigation is under way, and action will be initiated against those responsible in accordance with the law, TG SAFE said. They further added that stocking APIs for sale without a valid drug licence is punishable under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, with imprisonment of up to five years. TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing is responsible for issuing licences for the stocking and sale of APIs under the Act. 1a8dffc89945a4da.title: Healthy habits, preventive care key to youth wellbeing, says surgeon
1a8dffc89945a4da.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:03 am IST - CHENNAI Cardiac surgeon, healthcare innovator and author Shriram Nene interacts with moderator Vasanthi Hariprakash during a session at the Next Gen Forum. | Photo Credit: Johan Sathya Das J Preventive healthcare and emotional wellbeing must become an integral part of nurturing the next generation, said cardiothoracic surgeon and healthcare innovator Shriram Nene at the NextGen Forum, a two-day conclave on youth safety and wellbeing, which concluded in Chennai on Saturday. Delivering the keynote address titled ‘Before They Become Patients: Why Wellbeing Must Begin Young’, Dr. Nene spoke about the importance of developing healthy habits and prioritising preventive healthcare from an early age. Drawing on his experience in healthcare and his recently released book, ‘21 Days to Good Health’, he highlighted the need to make everyday wellbeing a priority rather than focusing on healthcare only after the onset of illness. He also spoke about the role of emotional wellbeing in ensuring that young people grow up healthy. Organised by The Kindness Foundation on November 13 and 14, the forum brought together over 200 students aged 11 to 17 from more than 20 schools and over 25 experts from 15 sectors. The two-day event featured discussions on youth safety, mental health, digital risks, substance misuse and the challenges faced by young people. The insights from the conclave will contribute to a co-created White Paper on Youth Safety and Wellbeing, which will include young people’s perspectives and recommendations from experts for families, institutions and policymakers, said foundation founder and managing trustee Mahima Poddar. 72599b68cc6a8b03.title: TGPCB recommends closures, forfeitures over dusty construction
72599b68cc6a8b03.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 02:11 am IST The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district. After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution control measures. The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution. Several violations of environmental norms were also identified, the TGPCB stated. The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects. After examining the severity of the violations, committee recommended the issuing of closure orders against projects where serious violations were identified, along with the forfeiture of bank guarantees. The committee also recommended forfeiture of bank guarantees in respect of projects where minor violations were observed. A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations. Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated. The committee recommended the issuance of closure orders against these projects, it added. Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders. A Ready Mix Concrete plant operating in association with another construction project was found to be functioning without obtaining Consent for Operation (CFO) from the TGPCB. ac44e8808ec5166e.title: AIADMK to protest seeking action against Deputy Speaker in Thuraiyur ‘assault’ incident
ac44e8808ec5166e.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:22 am IST - CHENNAI AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami. | Photo Credit: E. LAKSHMI NARAYANAN The AIADMK has announced a protest on November 18, demanding action over an alleged incident in which M. Ravisankar, the TVK MLA for Thuraiyur and Deputy Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assaulted a social activist. In a statement, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami alleged that Karthik Kumar, a social activist who went to meet Mr. Ravisankar to submit grievances, was subjected to a “brutal attack” and “verbal abuse”. Mr. Palaniswami further claimed that after evidence of the assault surfaced, Mr. Ravisankar threatened the activist again and used a police officer to coerce the victim into posting on social media that the incident had never occurred. He remarked that this demonstrated how brazenly TVK legislators were engaging in hooliganism, which surpassed even what was depicted in films. Criticising Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue, Mr. Palaniswami announced that the AIADMK would stage a condemnation protest at 10 a.m. on Wednesday (November 18 near the Anna Statue at the Thuraiyur bus stand, demanding strict action against Mr. Ravisankar. c2eea6fd68b63e51.title: Flood-prone areas to be monitored using drones in Chennai
c2eea6fd68b63e51.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai Residents in low-lying and flood-prone neighbourhoods across Chennai could be monitored more closely during the Northeast monsoon, with the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) planning to deploy drones across all 15 zones for 30 days, to help officials assess conditions on the ground. The initiative is intended to help civic officials keep track of vulnerable locations during periods of heavy rain and improve coordination of response measures. Aerial footage will allow officials to assess the situation in areas that may be difficult to monitor from the ground and identify locations requiring attention. Under the proposed arrangement, one drone and a trained operating team will be stationed in each of the city’s 15 zones, covering the northern, central, and southern regions. The teams will coordinate with zonal officials on the locations to be monitored and the timing of operations, according to officials. Live video feeds will be made available to designated GCC officials, while recorded footage will be handed over for subsequent assessment. The recordings will include details such as the date, time, zone, and location, wherever available. The footage is expected to support officials in assessing ground conditions in vulnerable neighbourhoods and in coordinating their response during the monsoon. The deployment will cover 30 days, with the operating teams required to follow the locations and priorities identified by GCC officials. 10fdc4f1014ce468.title: VIT-A.P. researchers demonstrate low-cost photonic tech for non-invasive disease screening
10fdc4f1014ce468.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:45 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Scientists from CATS Global (CASTLE Advanced Technologies and Systems), Nashik, Maharashtra, and VIT-A.P. University, Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, have developed and demonstrated an innovative, low-cost optical sensing approach that could pave the way for affordable, non-invasive disease screening through breath analysis. According to a press release from the VIT-A.P., the research article titled ‘Photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting of exhaled-breath metabolites for non-invasive disease screening’, authored by professors Rao Tatavarti, Sridevi Nadimpalli and P. Arulmozhivarman Pachiyappan, was published on November 6, 2026, in the international journal Scientific Reports, published by Springer Nature. The study explores a photonic sensing technique that uses a simple, low-power laser and a position-sensitive optical detector to identify distinctive optical signatures associated with disease-related chemical compounds. According to the release, human breath contains hundreds of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other gases that can reflect changes in the body’s metabolic processes. Variations in the concentration of these compounds can be associated with different diseases, making breath analysis a promising approach for non-invasive health screening. However, conventional breath-analysis technologies often rely on sophisticated laboratory instruments, including mass spectrometers, gas chromatographs and advanced optical spectroscopy systems, which can be expensive and require specialised infrastructure. The study addresses this challenge, by demonstrating the potential of photonic elastic-backscatter fingerprinting to detect, distinguish and classify different disease-associated gas mixtures through subtle changes in the intensity and spatial position of scattered laser light. This approach offers a direction towards developing compact, cost-effective and potentially portable optical sensing systems,

9fad22104d19b253.title: Past weather trends show fewer cyclones crossing Tamil Nadu coast during Northeast monsoon
9fad22104d19b253.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI Senior meteorologists point out that only 22 of the 117 cyclonic systems that formed over the Bay of Bengal during October and November, between 1981 and 2025, made landfall along the State’s coast. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B Tamil Nadu has seen relatively fewer cyclonic systems crossing its coast during the Northeast monsoon in the past 45 years, noted meteorologists. The Bay of Bengal is churning its next cyclone for the season. However, the current predictions indicate the possibility of only less rainfall over the State. Senior meteorologists point out that only 22 of the 117 cyclonic systems that formed over the Bay of Bengal during October and November, between 1981 and 2025, made landfall along the State’s coast. Many of the systems moved northwards towards places such as Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal, Bangladesh and the Arakan coast, while others weakened over the sea without crossing any coast. Y.E.A. Raj, former deputy director general of meteorology, Regional Meteorological Centre, Chennai, said 68 of the 117 systems moved north of Tamil Nadu towards the neighbouring States or countries, while 26 dissipated over the Bay of Bengal without making landfall. However, the State has received rainfall during some past years when the system dissipated over the sea. Citing IMD data, he said of the three to four weather systems or cyclones that generally form over the Bay of Bengal between October and December, only one comes closer to or crosses the Tamil Nadu coast. Going by statistics since 1981, Tamil Nadu experiences a coastal crossing roughly once every two years during October and November. The occurrence of three weather systems moving north of Tamil Nadu during October and November is not unprecedented. A similar pattern was recorded in 10 previous years, including 1983, 1996, 2010 and 2013, Mr. Raj added. Published - November 15, 2026 01:00 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscribe

095d608f305cb939.title: Tamil Nadu unlikely to see significant impact of severe cyclonic storm brewing over Bay of Bengal
095d608f305cb939.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 12:46 am IST - CHENNAI The current weather predictions indicate that the well marked is expected to gain strength as a cyclonic storm and intensify further as a severe cyclonic storm. | Photo Credit: VELANKANNI RAJ B The weather system brewing over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. However, Tamil Nadu may remain largely on the fringes of its impact, according to the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC). The season’s third cyclone is also likely to bypass Tamil Nadu and impact coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. The current weather predictions indicate that the well marked low-pressure area over southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to gain strength as a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal around November 16 evening. It is likely to further intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by November 18. While the weather agency is likely to provide clarity on the system’s movement and likely landfall location only after it consolidates into a depression, heavy rainfall warnings has been largely issued for other States, including Andaman and Nicobar islands, coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, till November 20. The cyclone is likely to be named ‘Akvan’, suggested by Iran under the naming list of tropical cyclones over North Indian Ocean. Officials of the RMC said the possibility of heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu remained low, given the system’s current position and expected trajectory. Rainfall of light to moderate intensity is likely to be concentrated over the southern and Western Ghats districts till November 20. V.R. Durai, Head, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, RMC, said there was currently no indication of heavy rainfall over the State. Winds from Arabian sea and a minor system over south Tamil Nadu would trigger rainfall over the southern and Western Ghats districts. Major weather disturbances usually form in the southwest Bay of Bengal duri

42450c98eac177bc.title: SCoR, Central Bank of India ink pact to extend welfare facilities for railway staff
42450c98eac177bc.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 11:49 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Officials of the South Coast Railway (SCoR), Vijayawada Division, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Central Bank of India, for extending more welfare facilities to railway employees. Additional Divisional Railway Manager (ADRM-Infrastructure) P. E. Edwin and Central Bank of India, Hyderabad Region, General Manager M. Pichai signed the MoU on Friday, aimed at providing enhanced financial and banking facilities to the employees. As per the MoU, railway employees are eligible for salary accounts with zero balance, personal accident and term insurance coverage up to ₹1.5 crore and other benefits. SCoR Vijayawada Division Senior Personal Officer Prem Kumar Lakhawat, bank Vijayawada regional head E. Venkateswara Rao, Guntur regional head G. V. Ramana Rao and other officials were present. 282873a6223dae89.title: Manipur probe panel gets sixth extension; no sign of report yet
282873a6223dae89.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:12 am IST - NEW DELHI The panel is probing the sequence of events and facts relating to the ethnic violence that broke out in the State on May 3, 2023, after a “Tribal Solidarity March” was organised in the hill districts. File | Photo Credit: ANI The three-member Commission of Inquiry, set up by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to probe the 2023 Manipur ethnic violence, was given a sixth extension on Friday. The Ministry notified that the commission, which was constituted on June 4, 2023, “shall submit its report to the Central government as soon as possible but not later than May 20, 2027”. More than 300 people have been killed in the ethnic violence that erupted between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people on May 3, 2023. Around 60,000 people have been displaced from their homes. The probe panel’s report is awaited even as the ethnic conflict has now spread to the Kuki and Naga communities. Since February this year, more than 60 people have been killed in Naga-Kuki clashes. The commission is now headed by former Supreme Court judge Balbir Singh Chauhan, after Ajai Lamba, the former Chief Justice of the Gauhati High Court, resigned as the chairperson of the panel in February this year. The panel is yet to finalise its report. Justice (retd.) Chauhan is also heading the judicial inquiry into an incident of violence that occurred in Ladakh’s Leh city on September 24, 2025 where four civilians, including a Kargil war veteran, were killed in police firing. The Ladakh report is yet to be submitted to the government. Manipur’s Commission of Inquiry has received around 11,000 affidavits. President’s rule was imposed in the State on February 13, 2025 and on February 4 this year, a new Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh took oath, ending Central rule. 4270f71143f5b115.summary: India's forex reserves increased by USD 2.49 billion to USD 719.547 billion during the week ended November 6, according to the RBI data released on Friday. In the previous week, the forex reserves had dropped by USD 2.691 billion to USD 717.056 billion. The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but had been on a decline ever since. During the week ended November 6, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, increased by USD 232 million to USD 591.350 billion, according to the data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 09a099c026b5c94a.title: Rajya Sabha panel visits ISRO, HAL facilities in Bengaluru
09a099c026b5c94a.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:41 am IST - Bengaluru The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies. | Photo Credit: K. Murali Kumar Members of the Subordinate Legislation Committee of Rajya Sabha on Friday visited key defence, space and finance institutions in Bengaluru as part of a study visit. The committee, led by Chairman Milind Deora, visited the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), toured the LCA Tejas Division and witnessed a static display of the defence PSU’s various platforms. The HAL said the committee reviewed the implementation of the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility) Rules, 2014. “HAL Chairman Ravi K., and Director (HR), M.G. Balasubrahmanya, and other senior officials were present during the interaction, which provided an opportunity to showcase the HAL’s contributions to indigenous aerospace development and its commitment to impactful and sustainable CSR initiatives,” the HAL said. The committee also visited the Indian Space Research Organisation’s U.R. Rao Satellite Centre which is the county’s lead centre for building satellites and developing associated satellite technologies. “The committee got a closer look at India’s satellite capabilities and discussed the future of our space sector from liberalisation and reusable rockets to Chandrayaan missions, space debris and e-waste regulations. While India’s space ambitions are reaching new heights, our sustainability game must keep up. Innovation and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” Mr. Deora posted on X. The committee also held meetings with officials of the Reserve Bank of India and leading Public Sector Unit (PSU) banks to discuss the future of digital payment security. 2a18505d20b9e62f.title: Former MIDS Director P.G. Babu no more
2a18505d20b9e62f.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:31 am IST - Chennai P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT P.G. Babu, former Director, Madras Institute of Development Studies, passed away in Dindigul, his hometown, on Thursday. He was 65 and is survived by his mother, a brother, and a sister. Prof. Babu was serving as the Vice-Chancellor of Vidyashilp University, Bengaluru, since 2023. During his tenure as the Director of MIDS between 2019 and 2022, he brought out a series of books in both Tamil and English, most notably on the economic policy during the pandemic. For over three decades, he had served at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research, Mumbai, where he was also the Dean of Graduate Studies and coordinated the Law and Economics programmes. His research focussed on Microeconomic theory and Game theory with applications across Environmental and Natural Resource Economics, Law and Economics, and Politics-Philosophy and Economics. His research contributions include work on the decision-making framework for climate change as part of the IPCC working group, which earned him a citation from the Prime Minister of India. 0833c1b532f61694.title: Germany open to discussing critical mineral partnerships with India, says Ambassador
0833c1b532f61694.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 12:01 am IST - COIMBATORE German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck (right) visited the Gedee Technical Training Institute in Coimbatore city on Friday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRAGEMENT Germany’s Ministry of Economic Affairs has critical mineral partnerships already with a range of countries. With India, the channels are open to discuss how to enhance the cooperation in that domain, German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck told The Hindu in Coimbatore on Friday. Asked about increasing recycling of industrial waste in European countries and its impact on raw material supplies to Indian companies, he said Germany also supports the Indian government in promoting and making progress in recycling and recovering industrial waste. One aspect, for example, is recycling of old solar panels because the raw materials are needed and China is increasing its export curbs. Germany is ready to further engage with India on critical minerals in order to work on sustainable solutions and securing supply chains. India and Germany share the destiny of being short of critical minerals. Circular economy is a strong part of the India-Germany Green and Sustainable Development Partnership. It will be further enhanced. But, the thrust is to support India in increasing its own recycling quota, the Ambassador said. Mr. Wieck, who visited the Gedee Technical Training Institute (GTTI) in Coimbatore, said, “Germany is keen on sharing its experience in vocational training with India. In the framework of our development cooperation, we have many programmes that encourage Indian companies to provide for training on the spot in close cooperation, for instance, with Indian technical institutes,” he said. Germany already recognises Indian dual vocational training certificates thereby enabling a smooth transition into the German labour market, if needed. f647fe46dbf1ca20.title: ABB India Q3CY26 results: Net profit rises 11% to ₹440 cr, revenue up 19.4%
f647fe46dbf1ca20.summary: Electrification and automation major ABB India on Friday posted an 11 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 440 crore in the September quarter compared to the year-ago period, driven by higher revenues. The company follows a January-December fiscal year. The net profit was Rs 398 crore in the quarter ended on September 30, 2025, an exchange filing showed. Revenues from operations rose to Rs 3,738 crore in the quarter from Rs 3,130 crore in the same period a year ago. ABB India Managing Director Sanjeev Sharma said, "We delivered a strong third quarter, with record Q3 orders, revenue growth and a healthy backlog reflecting continued customer confidence in ABB's technology and solutions." He stated that the demand remained broad-based across industries, supported by investments in productivity, energy efficiency and sustainable growth. Looking ahead, he stated that India's structural growth drivers in industrialisation, electrification, digitalisation and the energy transition continue

f3a26d1288f5f710.title: Vigilance Awareness Week concludes at NLCIL
f3a26d1288f5f710.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 05:30 am IST - CUDDALORE Prasanna Kumar Acharya, Chairman and Managing Director of NLCIL, presenting the Most Vigilant Employee Award to an employee at the valedictory function in Cuddalore on Thursday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Prasanna Kumar Acharya, chairman and managing director of NLC India Limited (NLCIL) has called for greater transparency and visibility in organisational systems in NLCIL, and the elimination of manual interventions. He was speaking at the valedictory function of the Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 in Neyveli on Thursday. Speaking at the meeting, Mr. Acharya said that contract manuals and operational procedures were being updated to strengthen accountability and ensure seamless governance. He appreciated the Vigilance Division’s outreach and preventive initiatives organised under the Central Vigilance Commission’s (CVC) theme, ‘Probity for Prosperity’. Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) Appakannu Govindarajan said that this year’s CVC guidelines reflected a shift from focusing on corruption to proactively promoting integrity, honesty, and probity. With NLCIL preparing for large-scale expansion, reducing procedural errors, strengthening capacity building, and keeping pace with technological advances were essential for innovation and sustained growth, a press release quoted him as having said. Highlighting public participation in the campaign, Mr. Govindarajan said reels and rangoli competitions had attracted people from different sections of society. He also stressed the contribution of employees and students to societal development. Director (Mines) Suresh Chandra Suman recalled Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s contribution to nation-building and commended the Vigilance Division for involving the public in the campaign. A special edition of NLCIL’s in-house vigilance magazine, Neyveli Vigil, was released on the occasion. Mr. Acharya, functional directors Samir Swarup, Rajesh Pratap Singh Sisodia, P.L.S.S. Chaitanya

e4645697523cef00.summary: India, the world's second-largest gold consumer, relies heavily on imports to meet demand | Image: Bloomberg India's merchandise trade deficit widened to a one-year high of $39.88 billion in October, exceeding forecasts as festive-season gold purchases and higher energy ​costs drove up imports. The deficit topped the $32.25 billion forecast in a Reuters ​poll and widened from $30.21 billion in September. The trade deficit last hit a record $42.58 billion in October ‌2025. Gold imports nearly tripled to $5.51 billion from $1.8 billion in September, as jewellers and consumers stepped up purchases ahead of the Hindu festival of Diwali, when buying gold is considered auspicious. India, the world's second-largest gold consumer, relies heavily on imports to meet demand. Mid-month, India's market regulator nudged asset management firms to halt bulk purchases of gold exchange-traded funds to limit investment demand for gold-backed products. A senior official said the recovery in gold imports this month was likely driven by a correction in global prices and pre-festive demand, though trade flows are influenced by multiple factors. India, the world's third-largest oil consumer after the United States and China, has also faced higher import costs due to energy-market disruptions caused by ‌the Middle East conflict. India imports nearly 85% of its crude needs. Brent crude futures have since fallen to around $95 a barrel, offering relief amid hopes of de-escalation following the Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections. Merchandise exports rose to $49.47 billion in October, up from the $44.40 billion of the previous month, government data showed, while imports rose to $89.35 billion against $74.61 billion in September. 4261476b303c73f9.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
4261476b303c73f9.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 01:24 am IST - NEW DELHI The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%. File image used for representation | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026). The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%. Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said. All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites. The SDCs have been instructed to strictly monitor compliance across the supply chain and healthcare facilities to ensure that the benefits of the revised maximum retail prices (MRPs) are passed on to patients. Any violation of the directive may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of the DPCO, 2013, the release noted. Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

a85d2bf44a8cf4e9.title: Edelweiss Financial Services Q2 FY27 results: Profit rises 18% to ₹207 cr
a85d2bf44a8cf4e9.summary: Edelweiss Financial Services on Friday reported an 18 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 207 crore for the second quarter ended September. The company had earned a profit of Rs 175 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal. Total income increased to Rs 2,602 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 1,900 crore in the year-ago period, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing. Interest income rose to Rs 720 crore from Rs 687 crore in the same quarter a year ago. During the quarter, total expenses also rose to Rs 2,393 crore from Rs 1,946 crore in the same period a year ago. The company completed the Rs 1,200-crore IPO of its subsidiary Edelweiss Alternatives last month. Earlier this year, global investment management firm Carlyle became a strategic majority investor in another subsidiary of the company, Nido Home Finance, with an investment of Rs 2,000 crore.

054e4d7fccd674ae.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:44 am IST - Chennai Bharathidasan Institute of Management (BIM), in collaboration with the University of Texas at Arlington (UTA) in the U.S., on Friday announced the launch of the Master of Science programme in Artificial Intelligence for Business (MSAIB), which is aimed at working professionals in India. On Friday, representatives of the two institutions exchanged Memoranda of Understanding for the course. The first batch of the course will start in August 2027. The first cohort will include 25 students, mostly working professionals, who are keen to upgrade their skills to secure better job opportunities in multinational companies, and the tuition fee is indicated to be around $27,000. Asit K. Barma, Director, BIM, told presspersons in Chennai that the classes would be held at the IIT-Madras Research Park. The location, being a technology hub, will be beneficial to students in terms of access to industry interactions. The conventional MBA course had, over the past few years, been losing its shine gradually, indicated by the falling enrolment for the Common Admission Test (CAT). Last year, there was a 2% drop in students taking the Common Admission Test compared to the previous year, Dr. Barma said. The two-year MSAIB course will provide an opening for young professionals to pursue an industry-oriented course, he said. Fernando Jaramillo, Associate Dean, College of Business, UTA, said the course would be offered in hybrid mode, with faculty members from the UTA visiting the Chennai campus for conducting classes. The curriculum for the course would be the same as the one offered at its Arlington campus. Radha K. Mahapatra, Chair and Professor, Information Systems and Operations Management, UTA, said the faculty for each course would spend about a week on the Chennai campus, while the rest of the classes would be conducted online. 7ef746d78b58d251.title: India imports over half its edible oil, faces food risks: NITI Aayog VC
7ef746d78b58d251.summary: India is perhaps still not secure regarding its food supply across the various products, as the country is the world's largest importer of edible oils, NITI Aayog vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said on Friday. Addressing an event here, Lahiri said India meets more than half of its edible oil needs through imports, and imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, valued at about USD 20 billion. Similarly, India is both the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses, and accounts for roughly a fourth of total global pulse consumption, approximately 25 to 27 million tonnes annually. "We are talking about Viksit Krishi in Viksit Bharat in 2047. As we move towards Viksit Bharat at 2047, are we secure regarding our food supply across the various products? Keerthana. According to details shared by Guidance, the discussion focused on accelerating the development of Grade-A office space and supporting infrastructure across the identified corridors to meet the needs of the state’s growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem. The roundtable brought together developers’ perspectives on strengthening these corridors as integrated destinations for GCC investment and growth. Tamil Nadu is home to more than 460 GCCs, including over 405 in Chennai, with the sector adding more than 55,000 jobs in 2025. Continued expansion by existing centres, alongside interest from new investors, has increased the need for readily available, high-quality office space. Participants discussed measures to accelerate project development, maintain competitive rentals and ensure that suitable space is available within the timelines required by global companies. Developers shared their perspectives on land availability, development costs, floor space index (FSI), approval processes and infrastructure requirements. The discussion emphasised the importance of developing complete GCC ecosystems in Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR), Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam Radial Road (PTR) and Mount–Poonamallee High Road (MPR) through mixed-use projects that integrate offices with housing, schools, healthcare, hospitality and retail. Public transport, last-mile connectivity and pedestrian access were identified as essential to supporting the growth of these corridors. Participants noted and appreciated the greater transparency and accountability they had experienced

5c01144be5e1a2d0.title: Modi comes to aid of elderly woman who felt unwell at Mysuru event
5c01144be5e1a2d0.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:02 am IST - MYSURU Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally came to the aid of an elderly woman who felt unwell during the inauguration of the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru on Friday. The woman, Prema Simbaiah, former president of Nanjangud Town Municipality and a BJP worker, appeared to feel dizzy and was on the verge of collapsing. Noticing her condition, Mr. Modi went up to her and ensured that she received immediate attention. She was given juice to help her recover. Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman was also present at the event. Mysuru district BJP president Subbanna later visited Ms. Simbaiah at her residence to enquire about her health. He said she was doing well. Thanking Mr. Modi for coming to her aid, Ms. Simbaiah said she had felt uncomfortable as she had not had lunch before arriving at the venue. She expressed her gratitude to the Prime Minister for providing her with juice and ensuring that she recovered. 9bad3be65f765bb1.title: Over 7,000 books removed from District Central Libraries in Vellore, nearby districts
9bad3be65f765bb1.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:39 am IST - VELLORE The library in Ranipet. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement As many as 7,995 books published by the controversial Agalvilakku and Phoenix Publications were removed from the racks of District Central Library in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts on Friday. The action comes against the backdrop of allegations of fake and AI-generated books being procured from these publishers for public libraries including Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore. “The identified books of the two publications were removed from the other books. The books, which are meant for distribution to branch libraries in the district for 2025-26, are stored in a separate room,” S. Valli, District Library Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu. Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications, followed by Tiruvannamalai (2,209 books), and Vellore (984 books). “Books on competitive examinations are a big attraction in District Central library as the facility has a large collection of books related to general knowledge,” said G. Satish, a reader. Officials said District Central Library in these districts have books on subjects including history, politics, law, economics, philosophy, agriculture, computer and mathematics. Reference books, especially for examinations conducted by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC), UPSC, and other competitive exams are available. As per norms, around 60,000 to 70,000 books are procured for each district library annually based on feedback provided by local librarians and readers. These books then distributed branch libraries in the district. As per estimates, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai have at least 120 branch libraries each whereas Ranipet and Tirupattur have around 50 branch libraries each. 599ef64f8dbe8628.title: Two men die as van rams tree in Tirupattur
599ef64f8dbe8628.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 12:41 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Two men and two cows killed after a van hit a roadside tree at Pudur village near Vaniyambadi town in Tirupattur on Friday. Police said K. Bhoopathy, 62, and V. Sankar, 28, both dairy farmers near Alangayam town, were taking the cows on the van to sell them at the weekly cattle market in Uthangarai village near Hosur. Bhoopathy’s son Manikandan, 28, and two other farmers Murugesan, 58, and Krishnan, 56, were also travelling with them. Police said that Manikandan lost control of the vehicle and rammed a roadside tree. In the impact, Manikandan and Sankar, sustained severe injuries and succumbed on the way to hospital. The two cows were killed. The other three men are under treatment. The incident occurred around 4 a.m. The Kavalur police have registered a case. f0d9913262eff5d1.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 06:22 am IST High Court of Delhi entrance gate. The Delhi High Court has taken suo motu cognisance of the condition of the Sriniwaspuri drain, citing its significant impact on waterlogging in the area and rampant illegal constructions on and around it. A Bench of Justice Prathiba M. Singh and Justice Manmeet P.S. Arora, while disposing of an appeal filed by residents of Sriniwaspuri, directed that the matter be converted into a fresh suo motu petition. The development came after the appellants, who had approached the court seeking proper maintenance, cleaning and reconstruction of drains in the area, sought permission to withdraw their appeal, stating that they did not wish to pursue the proceedings because of the continuous threats they were facing from local residents. In its November 5 order, the court allowed the appellants to withdraw their petition but made it clear that the larger public interest issues concerning the drain could not be ignored. “Owing to the large-scale impact of the drain on the general waterlogging in the area, as also the rampant illegal construction upon and around the drain, this is a fit case for the Court to not ignore the facts that have come to light in the various reports, including the recent inspection report of the Integrated Drain Management Cell (IDMC),” the court said. “Accordingly, the Court takes suo motu cognisance of the situation relating to the Sriniwaspuri drain. Let the inspection report filed by the IDMC and the status report filed by the DJB and other authorities in this case be moved to the new file of the writ petition titled ‘Re: Suo Motu Sriniwaspuri Drain’,” the court ordered. 97fc796799d8e5cb.title: Four-day Chhath festival begins in Bihar with Nahay Khay
97fc796799d8e5cb.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 01:10 am IST - PATNA Devotees arrive to offer prayers and take a holy dip in the Ganga River on 'Nahay Khay', the first day of Chhath Puja, in Patna on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: ANI Bihar’s famous Chhath festival began on Friday (November 13, 2026) with Nahay Khay on the first of four days of festivities. A large number of devotees gathered at ghats by rivers, including the Ganga, to collect water and bathe. The festival is performed with piety and the strict observance of fasts to express gratitude to the Sun God for sustaining life on Earth. There are no formal rituals or priests present, and devotion is central to the prayers. The people of Purvanchal (eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand) celebrate Chhath Puja on a grand scale. On the first day, all Chhath vratis (devotees holding fasts) bathe in the morning and offer prayers to the rising Sun before partaking in rice and pumpkin curry. On the second day, Kharna, roti and kheer are cooked as prasad in the evening, followed by two continuous days of fasting. On the third day, devotees offer arghya (obeisance) to the setting Sun at the ghats of rivers or temporary water bodies created by the State government, continuing their fast. The Chhath festival this year will conclude on November 16 after devotees offer arghya to the rising Sun on the fourth day, marking the end of the fast. Out of 103 ghats in Patna, 90 have been declared safe for devotees, while 13 have been declared unsafe this year. Chhath Puja is also being celebrated in over a dozen parks in Patna, which already have fountains and water bodies, including Eco Park, Harding Park, Naveen Sinha Park, Lal Bahadur Shastri Park, AG Colony Park, Urja Park, CID Colony Park, and Lohia Nagar Park, and the lake at the Patna Zoo. 406209c89fb3f98c.title: Man held for setting house on fire in Vellore
406209c89fb3f98c.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:01 am IST - VELLORE The house that was gutted. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A 54-year-old man was arrested by the Veppankuppam police on charges of setting on fire his daughter’s house at Agaram village near Odugathur town at foothills of Jawadhu Hills in Vellore on Friday. Police said the accused R. Anandan, 54, a wage labourer, was upset over his daughter Vaishnavi marrying Rajesh, a milk van driver, against his wishes. In a fit of rage, Anandan allegedly set on fire Rajesh’s father Kumar’s house in Agaram village. Residents alerted Veppankuppam police, who rushed to the spot with firefighters. The house, which was unoccupied, was gutted. A case was registered and Anandan was arrested. 7f05c1744b84c178.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said steps taken in the last decade helped the country to sail through the crisis emerged during the war in the Middle East. He was inaugurating various welfare projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore here, including renewable energy and petroleum infrastructure. "War around Iran and Gulf countries shows how important energy security is. Steps taken for energy security in the last decade helped the country face the crisis with resilience," the PM said. Regarding the Metro Pink Line, which was dedicated to the public, Modi said it gives better connectivity to people in Bengaluru. He also noted that the Metro rail network increased from 17 km in 2014 to over 100 km in 2026 in Bengaluru. On the occasion, Modi lauded Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav for serving the nation as the widow of a Kargil war hero.

The top-scoring 2.5 lakh candidates in JEE-Main are allowed to appear for JEE-Advanced. "The Joint Entrance Exam (JEE)-Advanced will be held on May 23, 2027," an official notification said. "The candidates appearing for JEE-Advanced will have the provision of using an on-screen basic (non-scientific) calculator with a 10-12 digit display," it added. Aspirants are allowed a maximum of two attempts in two consecutive years. The first attempt must be taken in the year of passing Class 12 and the second attempt in the following consecutive year.

88274b4b7367c7de.title: Bengal draft voter list on Nov 23, final electoral rolls on Jan 16
88274b4b7367c7de.summary: The Election Commission will publish the draft electoral rolls for West Bengal on November 23, with the final voters' list scheduled to be released on January 16, 2027, as part of a Special Summary Revision (SSR), a statement said on Friday. The revision will be conducted with January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date, allowing those who turn 18 by then to enrol as voters, it said. According to the schedule announced by the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office, electors can submit claims and objections between November 23 and December 22. The disposal of applications will be completed by January 8. Special campaign days will be held at designated polling stations across the state on November 28 and 29, and December 5, 6, 12, 13, 19 and 20 to facilitate public participation, the statement said. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will be available at polling stations on these days to assist voters with fresh enrolment, correction of particulars and submission of claims and objections. Boot

cd2365c62a5f3777.summary: Updated - November 14, 2026 01:08 am IST India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment. 6be81aa7223ce5c1.summary: Essar Group's IT firm Black Box on Friday reported a 30.6 per cent increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 72.68 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, aided by growth in data centre and enterprise businesses. The Mumbai-headquartered company had posted a net profit of Rs 55.65 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing by the company. Black Box's revenue from operations rose 22.2 per cent to Rs 1,936.30 crore, up from Rs 1,584.59 crore in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, the profit and revenue rose 30 per cent and 13 per cent, respectively. Growth was driven by execution across hyperscale data centre infrastructure and enterprise solutions, supported by growing momentum in its technology products business, the company said in a statement. Black Box secured over USD 250 million in data centre orders in the first half of FY27. b8602c9e790f5ba7.title: Librarian P.V. Konnur felicitated on his 75th birth anniversary
b8602c9e790f5ba7.summary: Published - November 14, 2026 12:32 am IST - Bengaluru Friends, colleagues and admirers of P.V. Konnur, the library science professional and president of LIS Academy, Bengaluru, felicitated him on his 75th birth anniversary. The Amruta Mahotsava was held at the Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University on Thursday. Ramesh B., Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University, released the felicitation volume brought out in Prof. Konnur’s honour and he said that such a dedicated librarian is very hard to find today, and that Prof. Konnur is a role model for budding librarians. He observed that the librarian’s role has become more challenging, as students now have to be drawn back to libraries from their mobile phones. He urged Prof. Konnur to lead this movement and to help university libraries become experiential centres. 603400d77cfff554.title: India’s TB deaths fall 38% since 2015, outpacing global decline: WHO report
603400d77cfff554.summary: New Delhi: India has recorded a 38% reduction in tuberculosis (TB) mortality since 2015, outperforming the global decline of 35%, the Union health ministry said on Thursday. Highlighted in the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report 2026 released on Thursday, the findings also showed that the country achieved a 94% treatment success rate among drug-susceptible TB patients. According to the WHO report, India’s estimated TB mortality rate dropped from 280 per million people in 2015 to 180 per million in 2025. Meanwhile, a nationally representative TB prevalence survey conducted in 2025 by the Indian Council of Medical Research—National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (ICMR-NIRT) has been shared with the WHO. The findings are currently under technical review, after which the WHO will publish an updated country profile for India. The health ministry added that 96% of India’s TB programme funding requirements are now met through domestic resources. The ministry also highlighted how the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan has transformed detection through technological innovation. Between December 2024 and November 2026, more than 250 million people were brought under TB screening. Authorities conducted over 11 crore chest X-rays—using portable, AI-enabled diagnostic tools—alongside more than 30 million rapid molecular nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT). This identified 4.86 million new TB cases, including 1.49 million asymptomatic patients. The first intensified 100-day campaign under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 7 December 2024, across 347 high-priority districts in 33 states and Union territories before being expanded nationwide. A second intensified 100-day campaign was launched on 24 March 2026, focusing on screening in 158,000 high-risk villages and wards, congregate settings, and vulnerable populations. 9600c1ce84962ac5.summary: Hours after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tendered his resignation from the chief executive officer (CEO) position amid the spy affair scandal, US President Donald Trump said, "A legend should replace a legend," and endorsed former Apple Inc. chief executive Tim Cook's name. "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! (sic)," Trump said. While President Trump's public endorsement of Tim Cook drew widespread attention, neither Nvidia nor Apple has issued an official statement regarding Cook's potential cross-company migration Cook stepped down after a 15-year stint as Apple's CEO in September and is now executive chairman at the iPhone-maker. The tech giant has appointed the company's Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, as the interim CEO and said the "board has initiated a search for a permanent CEO." Nvidia has also restructured its governance, appointing Harvey C Jones as the company's first-ever Chair of the Board. Seeking to reassure investors ahead of its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results, scheduled for November 17, Jones said, “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Colette Kress also expressed confidence in the company's direction, stating, "We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead." Huang, who co-founded the tech giant, has been embroiled in the controversy ever since reports claimed he had an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. cfc2d43380d0d226.headline_en: No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules: CBDT
cfc2d43380d0d226.raw_facts: Updated cross-border tax dispute guidelines also clarify how treaty-level resolution interacts with domestic appeals, advance rulings, and settlement schemes under the Income Tax Act, 2025.
flags: Anachronism: The 'Income Tax Act, 2025' does not exist; the current governing law in India is the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Terminology Error: 'MAP relief' (Mutual Agreement Procedure) is a treaty-based mechanism, not typically described as 'relief' in the context of safe harbour rules, which are a separate domestic tax provision.

Logical Inconsistency: Safe harbour rules are a unilateral domestic mechanism to avoid transfer pricing adjustments, whereas MAP is a bilateral treaty mechanism. Stating 'No MAP relief for taxpayers using safe harbour rules' is conceptually confused, as safe harbour users generally do not face transfer pricing disputes that would require MAP.

6f68af2d20b39185.title: CPI(M) leader P. Rajeeve flays police action against protesters in Keralam’s Thiruvananthapuram
6f68af2d20b39185.summary: Published - November 13, 2026 12:30 am IST - KOCHI Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] central committee member P. Rajeeve has termed Wednesday night’s police action against protesters in Thiruvananthapuram and the removal to hospital of Valarmathi S., secretary of the action council and convener of the lower primary school teacher (LPST) rank holders’ protest committee, who was on a hunger strike, as anti-democratic. The government must specify which court order within six months of the United Democratic Front (UDF) assuming power that it relied on for such actions. Moreover, it owes an explanation on why it “went back” on an earlier assurance to extend the time frame for Public Service Commission rank lists. Agitations are being “suppressed”, while social media accounts are being closed down, he told the media here on Thursday. Likewise, the government that is finding fault with the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) is taking credit for projects that were taken up under it. In another move, the government is preparing to inaugurate the construction work of the KIIFB-funded digital park, whose foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi when the Left Democratic Front was in power in the State, Mr. Rajeeve said. df41bfe3c97cd415.title: Nitin Nabin, CM inaugurate 11-km Chhath ghat along Munak Canal

The project was completed at a cost of ₹115.29 crore, according to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO). Addressing the gathering, Mr. Nabin said ahead of the Chhath festival, Ms. Gupta presented a “major gift” to Chhath devotees, followers of the Sanatana Dharma, and the Purvanchal community. The project includes the construction of the Chhath ghat, service roads along both banks of the canal, bridges, road widening and beautification of the canal. More than 1,400 ghats are expected to be set up across the Capital this year for Chhath Puja, which will be celebrated on November 15 and 16, according to the Delhi government. People from Purvanchal, hailing from eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, constitute a significant voter base in Delhi and celebrate the festival, making it politically important every year. The Yamuna holds religious significance for the people of Purvanchal, who observe Chhath Puja by taking a holy dip in the river.
